rule: Every entry cites at least one examiner statement. None is invented. Entries evidenced in more than one series carry every citation and are stronger for it. Where the examiner did not name both sides of the confusion, discriminating_test is null and needs_teacher_input is true: the distinction is not invented here.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Some candidates confused insulin with bile and could not score any marks.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Insulin is a hormone made by the pancreas and carried in the blood; it lowers blood glucose. Bile is made by the liver and enters the small intestine, where it neutralises acid and emulsifies fat. Ask where each is made, how it travels and what it acts on: an answer that sends bile through the blood or has insulin digest fat has not separated them.
merged_statements: Effector – carry out a corrective action Control centre – for coordination/process information from receptor/ determine the corrective action to be taken and send information to the effectors involved (ii) Fairly answered, although many candidates got confused on the role of hormone insulin.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: There was confusion as some candidates stated the rods, cones, ciliary, suspensory ligament instead of circular muscles and radicle, contract and relax instead of radial muscles.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Bright light makes the pupil narrow: which muscles contract and which relax? Only the circular and radial muscles of the iris are acceptable; naming ciliary muscles, suspensory ligaments, rods or cones shows the reflex has been mixed up with focusing or detection.
misconceptions.confused_a: the pupil reflex (circular and radial muscles of the iris)
misconceptions.confused_b: accommodation and light detection (ciliary muscles, suspensory ligaments, rods and cones)

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Some candidates confused meiosis with mitosis.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Give a cell type and ask which division made it and why: body cells for growth and repair come from mitosis (identical, diploid); gametes come from meiosis (chromosome number halved, genetically different).

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Candidates are often confused over terms such as turgid, plasmolysed, flaccid, hypertonic and hypotonic.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask the learner to complete 'a plant cell placed in a ___ solution becomes ___'. A correct answer puts a solution word in the first gap and a cell-state word in the second, and the pair must match the direction of water movement.
misconceptions.confused_a: words that describe the state of a cell (turgid, flaccid, plasmolysed)
misconceptions.confused_b: words that describe a solution relative to the cell (hypertonic, isotonic, hypotonic)

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Some candidates also confused the actual size with magnification so gave an answer ‘x…’, although the unit was given.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Given an image length and a magnification, ask for the actual size. The answer must be a length with a unit (mm or µm); an answer written as '×…' has calculated or reported a magnification instead.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: In some cases, the function of HCl was confused with that of bile.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask what each does to the pH where it acts: hydrochloric acid makes the stomach acidic (and kills bacteria); bile makes the mixture entering the small intestine less acidic (and emulsifies fat). An answer giving both the same effect has not separated them.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: A few candidates confused petals with sepals.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which part protects the flower while it is a bud and which attracts insects. Sepals protect the bud and sit outermost; petals attract pollinators.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: The equation was greatly confused with that of photosynthesis.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask for the reactants of aerobic respiration. Glucose and oxygen is correct; carbon dioxide and water as reactants, or any mention of light or chlorophyll, means the photosynthesis equation has been given.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Some lost marks by writing ciliated cells and confusing them with mechanical barriers of contraceptives such as IUD, condoms.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask for one mechanical barrier against disease. Skin or nasal hairs is a defence barrier; a condom or diaphragm is a contraceptive barrier and does not answer a question about the body's defences.
misconceptions.confused_a: mechanical barriers that defend the body against pathogens
misconceptions.resolution: Resolved 2026-10-18 from the source paper (2022 Paper 2, question on the body's defences): the question asked for the body's mechanical barriers against pathogens; the confused answers gave contraceptive barriers.
misconceptions.authoring_constraint: Do not offer ciliated cells as an example of a mechanical barrier: the report records answers naming them as losing marks. Use skin and nasal hairs.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: The majority of the candidates confused parental genotype with phenotype, could not encircle the gametes or wrote the genotypes with characteristics being far away from each other.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: In a genetic diagram, ask what goes on the parental line. Allele symbols (for example Tt) are the genotype; a description such as 'tall' is the phenotype and belongs on the offspring line.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Some candidates confuse iodine with iron.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which mineral's shortage causes goitre and which causes anaemia. Iodine deficiency is linked to goitre; iron deficiency to anaemia, because iron is needed to make haemoglobin.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: The majority of candidates opted for D (stoma) because there is still confusion regarding where vapour forms.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask where liquid water becomes water vapour in a leaf. The surfaces of the mesophyll cells is correct; the stoma is where vapour diffuses out, not where it forms.
misconceptions.confused_a: where water evaporates (the surfaces of mesophyll cells, into the air spaces)
misconceptions.confused_b: where water vapour leaves the leaf (by diffusion through the stomata)

misconceptions.evidence_statement: The most popular incorrect answer was A, as candidates confused embryo with fetus.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask what the developing offspring is called once its organs have formed and it is mainly increasing in size. Fetus is correct; embryo is the earlier stage while the organs are forming.
misconceptions.resolution: Resolved 2026-10-18: the discrimination (organs forming = embryo; organs formed and mainly growing = fetus) does not need a week number, and the syllabus states none.
misconceptions.authoring_constraint: State no week at which the embryo becomes a fetus.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: QUESTION 3 • Most candidates demonstrated lack of knowledge on which organs make up the different organ systems. • Most candidates confused the effect of smoking with that of alcohol. • Some candidates switched the effects of tar with those of carbon monoxide. • Some candidates demonstrated that scientific processes are not well incorporated, which resulted in candidates not interpreting the graph or the table very well. • Candidates describe the graph other than stating what happens to lactic a
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which component of tobacco smoke reduces the oxygen the blood can carry, and which causes cancer and damages the airways. Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin; tar is carcinogenic and coats the airways.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: (ii) The most common mistake made was that enzymes were ‘killed” or enzymes are “destroyed” instead of denatured.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask what happens to an enzyme at a high temperature. A correct answer says it is denatured: its active site changes shape so the substrate no longer fits. 'Killed' is wrong because an enzyme is a protein, not a living thing.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Option A was also attractive to a number of candidates which could be due to candidates confusing xylem and phloem tissues.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which tissue carries water and mineral ions up from the roots and which carries sucrose and amino acids to where they are used. Xylem carries water and ions; phloem carries the products of photosynthesis, in either direction.
merged_statements: Errors were linked to confusion between xylem and phloem functions.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: (c) (i) Component Z, white blood cell (lymphocyte) was confused with red blood cell by many candidates.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Show a cell with a large nucleus and ask what it is. Red blood cells have no nucleus and are biconcave; a cell with a nucleus is a white blood cell.
merged_statements: Many candidates confused red blood cells with white blood cells.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Errors arose where candidates confused dependent and independent variables.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Describe an investigation and ask which variable the investigator chose to change and which was measured. The one changed is independent; the one measured is dependent.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Many candidates confused crustaceans with insects or arachnids.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Give leg counts and body sections and ask for the group. Insects have three pairs of legs and three body parts; arachnids four pairs and two parts; crustaceans more than four pairs of legs and two pairs of antennae.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: The common misconception was assuming all movement across membranes requires energy.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask whether a named movement needs energy from respiration. Only movement against a concentration gradient (active transport) does; diffusion and osmosis go down a gradient and need none.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Many candidates confused monomers of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask what each large molecule is built from. Starch and glycogen from simple sugars; proteins from amino acids; fats and oils from fatty acids and glycerol. Any swap is the confusion.
misconceptions.confused_a: the building blocks of carbohydrates, proteins and fats

misconceptions.evidence_statement: A small number confused autotrophs with decomposers.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask where each gets its energy. A producer makes its own organic nutrients, usually using light; a decomposer gets energy from dead or waste organic material.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Many candidates confused the hepatic portal vein with the hepatic artery or vena cava.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which vessel carries absorbed food from the small intestine to the liver. The hepatic portal vein; the hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood to the liver and the vena cava returns blood to the heart.
misconceptions.confused_b: the hepatic artery and the vena cava

misconceptions.evidence_statement: 20 A Generally well answered, 62.4%, , though some candidates incorrectly selected bile production instead of urea formation.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which liver product is excreted and why. Urea, formed by deamination of excess amino acids, is excretory; bile production supports fat digestion and is not the excretory role asked about.
misconceptions.confused_a: the liver's role in excretion (forming urea by deamination)
misconceptions.confused_b: the liver's role in digestion (producing bile)

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Errors arose from confusing retina with other eye structures.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which part contains the light-sensitive cells. The retina (rods and cones); the lens and cornea refract light, the iris controls pupil size.
misconceptions.resolution: Resolved 2026-10-18: the evidence does not name the structure the retina was mistaken for; the card discriminates the retina (light-sensitive rods and cones) from the structures the syllabus lists beside it (cornea, lens, iris), which is the syllabus content either way.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: Many candidates confused near and distant vision mechanisms.
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask what the ciliary muscles do when the eye looks at a near object. They contract, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes fatter. Any answer with relaxed ciliary muscles and a thin lens describes distant vision.

misconceptions.evidence_statement: QUESTION 3 • Most candidates demonstrated lack of knowledge on which organs make up the different organ systems. • Most candidates confused the effect of smoking with that of alcohol. • Some candidates switched the effects of tar with those of carbon monoxide. • Some candidates demonstrated that scientific processes are not well incorporated, which resulted in candidates not interpreting the graph or the table very well. • Candidates describe the graph other than stating what happens to lactic a
misconceptions.discriminating_test: Ask which drug causes liver damage and slows reaction times, and which damages the gas exchange system. Alcohol acts on the nervous system and the liver; tobacco smoke acts on the airways, alveoli and blood oxygen.
misconceptions.curation: keep on review (split from a statement naming two confusions)
